body.statement: Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the event that every empirical \((X,Z)\) cell is nonempty. Uniformly over \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal P\), \[\sup_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}P_n(\mathcal E_n^c)\le 2J(1-p_0\varepsilon)^n\longrightarrow0.\] On \(\mathcal E_n\), every denominator fallback in \(\widehat e_{n,x}\), \(\widehat q^d_{n,z,x,k}\), and \(\widehat\psi_{w,n}\) is inactive, and the totalized \(\widehat w_n\), \(\widehat v_n\), endpoint estimators, retained face family, multiplier process, critical value, and \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) equal their ordinary empirical-cell counterparts. Consequently totalization changes any coverage probability by at most \(2J(1-p_0\varepsilon)^n\) and does not alter the limit in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\).
body.justification: This proposition closes the finite-sample domain of every empirical and multiplier object without changing the uniform first-order experiment.
body.gap: Asymptotic cell-probability arguments often leave conditional empirical ratios undefined on empty cells; the explicit exponential bound makes the proposed whole-set procedure a genuine finite-sample map.
body.consumer: It permits software for sparse Job Corps covariate cells to return a deterministic interval on every dataset while preserving the theorem's uniform coverage guarantee.
